channel.title: NPR Topics: Economy
channel.description: Understand the economic forces shaping daily life. Follow NPR for stories on inflation, affordability, consumer spending and jobs, plus episodes of Planet Money and The Indicator.

item.title: Can luxury save Macy's?
item.description: This week's celebration of Macy's 100th Thanksgiving parade finds the department store at a turning point. After years of losing sales, the retailer is reimagining itself — as a higher-end destination.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Record spending expected on Black Friday
item.description: Americans are expected to spend more money on Black Friday than any other day this year. How is inflation and the current economic situation affecting that?
item.content:encoded: Americans are expected to spend more money on Black Friday than any other day this year. How is inflation and the current economic situation affecting that?

item.title: Why Americans are still Black Friday shopping despite strained wallets
item.description: NPR's A Martinez asks Georgia Tech Professor Chris Gaffney why Americans continue to spend during the holidays, despite trouble spots in the economy.
item.content:encoded: NPR's A Martinez asks Georgia Tech Professor Chris Gaffney why Americans continue to spend during the holidays, despite trouble spots in the economy.

item.title: Inflation is still hot, fueled in part by the AI boom
item.description: The U.S. economy grew at a rapid clip during the summer and early fall, due in part to the artificial intelligence boom. That boom is also fueling higher inflation and rattling the stock market.
item.content:encoded: The U.S. economy grew at a rapid clip during the summer and early fall, due in part to the artificial intelligence boom. That boom is also fueling higher inflation and rattling the stock market.
item.dc:creator: Scott Horsley

item.title: In a time of rising costs, one Thanksgiving commodity is cheaper: cannabis
item.description: Steep discounts for "Green Wednesday," one of the highest-selling days for cannabis, help customers keep costs down. But experts say retailers are feeling the pinch.

item.title: Many families are cutting corners at the grocery store to pay their other bills
item.description: Cash-strapped consumers are changing they way they spend money. As essentials like rent and utility bills gobble up more of their budget, some families are dialing back on groceries or eating out.

item.title: What should it cost to insure a home in wildfire country?
item.description: Some California homeowners have spent thousands making their homes safer from wildfires. Yet all that work has barely made a dent in their insurance bills. Should they be getting a bigger break?

item.dc:creator: Greg Rosalsky

item.title: From Wall Street to Main Street, how artificial intelligence is affecting the economy
item.description: Artificial intelligence is sending shock waves through the stock market, as investors try to predict how their big bets will pay off. Meanwhile some real businesses are putting AI to work, with mixed results.

item.title: Chief economist for Moody's Analytics on why Anthropic's IPO caused market volatility
item.description: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Mark Zandi, chief economist for Moody's Analytics, about Anthropic's Wall Street debut and why it seems to have triggered recent market volatility.

item.title: AI is making it hard for young people to find work, report says
item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with Matt Sigelman, president of the Burning Glass Institute, about a new report indicating that AI is already squeezing the job market for young jobseekers.
